pm_exper_user_1530_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I calm my mind enough to fall asleep when it keeps racing at night?
pm_exper_user_1530_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) When your mind is full of unfinished tasks, try setting aside ten minutes before bed to jot down everything on your mind, creating a sense of closure for the day. Afterwards, sit quietly in a comfortable spot and simply focus on your breath and the feeling of the present moment. Pair this with slow breathing to root yourself in calm before sleep.
(b) When your mind is full of unfinished design details, try setting aside ten minutes before bed to recite a few lines of classical Arabic poetry, allowing the rhythm and imagery to clear your thoughts. Afterwards, step into the courtyard or balcony to enjoy the cooling night air, absorbing the stillness like a desert oasis. Pair this with slow breathing to root yourself in calm before sleep.
(c) When your mind is full of unfinished design details, try setting aside ten minutes before bed to compose a short piece of music or hum a melody you’ve been working on. Afterwards, sit quietly by a window and listen to the sounds outside, letting each note replace the day’s mental noise. Pair this with slow breathing to root yourself in calm before sleep.
(d) When your mind is full of unfinished design details, try setting aside ten minutes before bed to sketch a ‘closing scene’ for the day’s work, much like a final flourish in a garden bed. Afterwards, step outdoors, even briefly, to breathe in the quiet night air and focus on the scent and texture of a single plant — this can help shift your thoughts from planning to presence. Pair this with slow breathing to root yourself in calm before sleep.
